# Form Foundry

Form Foundry edits procedural three.js assets and free PolyFork models in the browser. Fetch ./catalog.json for the starter catalog, including complete recipes. Its schema is at ./agent-schema.json. Both paths are relative to the deployed app.

## Self-describing exported GLBs

Every GLB exported from Form Foundry (both studio originals and imported PolyFork models) embeds a versioned capability manifest in its exported root node extras at `nodes[0].extras.formFoundry` (exposed by three.js `GLTFLoader` on `gltf.scene.children[0]?.userData.formFoundry`, or `gltf.scene.userData.formFoundry`; `inspectAsset(gltf.scene, gltf.animations)` discovers it automatically). Inspect it before placing a model in a scene so authored interactions are never lost:

- `riggedParts`: movable hinges and slides (`{ name, label, type: "rotate" | "slide", axis, range, describe }`). `0` is rest pose; `range` is the safe travel in degrees (`rotate`) or meters (`slide`).
- `detachableParts`: named groups (`{ name, label, describe }`) that can be hidden or removed cleanly with closed geometry behind them. Hidden detachable parts remain in the exported GLB and are hidden on load via `state.hiddenParts` when using `createAssetController`.
- `nightZones`: emissive night lighting zones (`{ name, label, color, intensity, albedo, describe }`) where `albedo` is a 6-digit sRGB hex matched against linear `COLOR_0` vertex colors after linear-to-sRGB conversion.
- `decals`: declared flat or curved sign/logo surfaces (`{ name, at, normal, up, size, describe }`).
- `colorZones`, `presets`, `dimensions` (`sizeM`, `originY`, `origin`), `physics` (`body`, `massKg`, `material`), `ik`, `clips` (including `synthesized: true` for baked part clips), and current `state` (`pose`, `hiddenParts`, `night`, `decalText`).

In a three.js scene, `dist/studio-sdk.js` exports `inspectAsset(group, animations?)`, `createAssetController(group)`, and `synthesizeRigClips(group)` so you can discover and drive any exported GLB or starter asset in one line:

    import { inspectAsset, createAssetController } from './studio-sdk.js';
    const info = inspectAsset(gltf.scene, gltf.animations); // discovers door, planter, night zones, decals, clips, size
    const ctrl = createAssetController(gltf.scene);
    ctrl.openPart('door');                                  // or ctrl.setPart('door', 80), ctrl.closePart('door')
    ctrl.setVisible('planter', false);                      // hide a detachable part
    ctrl.setNight(true);                                    // illuminate declared night zones

## Browser API

Open the studio and use window.forgeStudio.

- listTemplates() lists the available starters.
- getRecipe() reads the active starter recipe. Returns null while viewing an imported GLB.
- applyRecipe(recipe) validates and displays a complete starter recipe.
- save() saves the active asset to this browser's inventory.
- remix(name?) starts a separately named draft from the current model and edits. It keeps the active clip and camera. Call save() to add the copy to inventory, and call save() again to update that copy.
- listInventory() reads the browser's saved inventory.
- inspectModel() returns the active model's complete capability manifest (`riggedParts`, `detachableParts`, `nightZones`, `decals`, `presets`, `dimensions`, `physics`, `clips`, `paintSlots`, and current `state`).
- listParts() lists the active model's rigged parts (with current `value`) and detachable parts (with `visible`).
- setPartPose(name, value), openPart(name), closePart(name), setPartVisible(name, visible), setNightMode(on), and applyColorway(name) operate interactive features directly.
- exportGLB(options?) returns a Promise<ArrayBuffer> containing the active asset as a binary glTF file with `extras.formFoundry`. Pass `{ includePartClips: true }` to also bake standard glTF AnimationClips for rigged parts (for example `Open door`).
- listPaintSlots() enumerates the active GLB's editable colors as {id, label, color, originalColor, zoneName?}. Each color is an untinted six-digit sRGB value. Starter recipes have primary and accent colors instead.
- getImportEdits() and setImportEdits({name, tint, scale, proportion, paint?, pose?, hiddenParts?, night?, decalText?}) read and replace the loaded GLB's edits. Retain the other edits when patching one field.
- listClips() returns clip names and durations. playClip(index) previews a clip. Compatible humanoids include the packaged downloadable CC0 motion library. Both original characters also retain their two studio cycles. exportGLB() includes all available clips even before listClips() is called.
- openPolyfork(id, name) loads a free GLB and its public metadata directly from PolyFork and returns a Promise<void>.

To change a starter asset, read its recipe, replace the requested fields, apply the full recipe and save when the user requests persistence. Both colors take six-digit sRGB hex values. Scale and proportion are numbers in [0.65, 1.5]. The detail field toggles optional secondary parts. Quality selects the authored geometry level, either "standard" or "hd". All six catalog recipes use HD. Version 1 recipes that omit quality render at standard quality.

Example for the developer console

    const studio = window.forgeStudio;
    await studio.openPolyfork('village-shopfront-d3088e', 'Village Shopfront');
    const info = studio.inspectModel();
    studio.openPart('door');
    studio.setNightMode(true);
    const glb = await studio.exportGLB({ includePartClips: true });

## Upstream assets

Search the public PolyFork API for an asset id and title before calling openPolyfork. Form Foundry automatically fetches the free detail metadata and colorway schema when opening a PolyFork model. Form Foundry's starter recipes and PolyFork's model-specific creation parameters use separate formats.

- API overview: https://polyfork.dev/api
- Search example: https://polyfork.dev/api/assets?q=drone&free=1&per_page=5
- Agent instructions: https://polyfork.dev/prompt.txt
- Attribution and licensing: https://polyfork.dev/licensing
